title: HEP-TILE: HBV Whole Genome Sequencing (Nanopore Protocol)
author: Sheila Lumley
materials: Quantify using a Qubit or Quantus.

steps.title: Prepare PCR master mixes
steps.instruction: In a clean mastermix cabinet (wipe and UV‑sterilise before and after), set up two 25 µL PCR reactions per sample in strip‑tubes or a plate: add 12.5 µL Q5 Hot‑Start High‑Fidelity 2X Master Mix to each; for Reaction 1 add 2.5 µL V3 Pool 1 (10 µM) and 0 µL V3 Pool 2, for Reaction 2 add 0 µL V3 Pool 1 and 2.5 µL V3 Pool 2; add 7.5 µL nuclease‑free water to each; add DNA volume based on viral load (VL): if VL > 5 log10 IU/mL add 2.5 µL DNA to each reaction, if VL < 5 log10 IU/mL add 7 µL DNA (adjust water accordingly to keep total 25 µL). For very low VL (<3 log10 IU/mL) run duplicate reactions. Gently mix by pipetting and pulse‑spin to collect liquid.

steps.title: Add DNA to PCR reactions
steps.instruction: In the DNA/sample addition cabinet (wipe and UV‑sterilise before and after), add the appropriate volume of extracted DNA to each PCR reaction as described above, mix gently by pipetting and pulse‑spin to collect liquid at the bottom of the tube.

steps.title: Program thermal cycler
steps.instruction: Load the following program: Heat activation 98 °C 30 s (1 cycle); Denaturation 98 °C 15 s (35 cycles if VL > 5 log10 IU/mL, otherwise 40 cycles); Annealing 65 °C 5 min (same number of cycles as denaturation); Hold 4 °C indefinitely.

steps.title: Combine PCR pools
steps.instruction: Label the strip‑tubes/plate, then combine 25 µL of the Reaction 1 product (Pool 1) with 25 µL of the Reaction 2 product (Pool 2) for each sample to give a 50 µL combined amplicon. Perform this step in the post‑PCR cabinet (wipe and UV‑sterilise before and after).

steps.title: Normalize amplicon input
steps.instruction: In a new PCR strip‑tube or plate, set up a reaction for each sample normalising to 80 ng amplicon DNA input; include one reagent‑only negative control. (Exact component volumes are as defined in the downstream kit protocol.)

steps.title: Quantify barcoded amplicons
steps.instruction: Using a fluorometer (Qubit or Quantus), quantify 1 µL of each barcoded amplicon. Aim for at least 30 ng total pooled amplicon to achieve maximum run yield.

steps.title: Set up adapter ligation
steps.instruction: In a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube, combine 30 µL barcoded amplicon pool, 10 µL NEBNext Quick Ligation Reaction Buffer (5X), 5 µL adaptor mix (NA), and 5 µL Quick T4 DNA Ligase. Mix gently; total volume 50 µL.

steps.title: Mix library beads
steps.instruction: Immediately before use, thoroughly mix the library beads by pipetting; they should be mixed right before loading. (From experience, 20 ng library can be loaded successfully.)

steps.title: Resuspend lyophilised oligos
steps.instruction: If making primer pools from individual oligos, fully resuspend each lyophilised oligo in 1× TE to a concentration of 100 µM, vortex thoroughly and spin down.

steps.title: Dilute primer stocks
steps.instruction: Dilute each 100 µM primer pool 1:10 in molecular‑grade water to obtain 10 µM primer stocks. Primers are used at a final concentration of 15 nM per primer; therefore add ~2.5 µL of the 10 µM pool to each 25 µL PCR reaction. Prepare multiple 100 µL aliquots of the 10 µM stocks and freeze for future use.

steps.title: Create primer pools
steps.instruction: Sort all odd‑region primers into one rack and add 5 µL of each odd‑region primer to a 1.5 mL tube labelled “Pool 1 (100 µM)”. Repeat for all even‑region primers into a tube labelled “Pool 2 (100 µM)”. Perform pooling in the mastermix cabinet (wipe and UV‑sterilise before and after).

steps.title: Prepare DNA sample plates
steps.instruction: Prepare 11–94 DNA samples plus one nuclease‑free water negative control per library (add a second negative control at the start of library prep). Batch samples by viral load (above or below 5 log10 IU/mL). If samples were frozen, vortex briefly and pulse‑spin; keep all samples on ice. Include a positive control (e.g., NIBSC HBV control) if desired.

steps.title: SPRI bead cleanup (0.8×)
steps.instruction: Add 40 µL SPRI beads to the 50 µL pooled PCR product (0.8× ratio). Gently mix and incubate 5 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Magnetic separation
steps.instruction: Place the tube on a magnetic rack for 2 min (or until the supernatant is clear). Discard the supernatant.

steps.title: First ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL room‑temperature 70 % ethanol to the bead pellet, gently bathe the pellet, then discard the ethanol without disturbing the beads.

steps.title: Second ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Repeat the 100 µL 70 % ethanol wash exactly as above.

steps.title: Remove residual ethanol
steps.instruction: Pulse‑centrifuge to collect any remaining liquid, then remove residual ethanol with a P10 pipette. Ensure all ethanol is removed.

steps.title: Air‑dry beads
steps.instruction: With the tube lid open, air‑dry the bead pellet for 1–2 min, or until it loses its shine. Do not over‑dry.

steps.title: Elute DNA from beads
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried pellet in 20 µL nuclease‑free water, mix gently, and incubate 2 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Collect eluate
steps.instruction: Place the tube back on the magnetic rack until the solution is clear, then transfer the supernatant (clean PCR product) to a new labelled tube, avoiding any beads.

steps.title: Prepare end‑prep master mix
steps.instruction: Make a master mix for end‑preparation: up to 8.3 µL clean PCR product, 1.2 µL Ultra II End‑Prep Reaction Buffer, 0.5 µL Ultra II End‑Prep Enzyme Mix, and nuclease‑free water to a final volume of 10 µL per reaction. Aliquot into strip‑tubes/plate.

steps.title: End‑prep incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the end‑prep reactions sequentially: 15 min at room temperature, 15 min at 65 °C, then 1 min on ice.

steps.title: Set up native barcode ligation
steps.instruction: In a new PCR strip‑tube/plate, add per sample: 1 µL end‑prep reaction, 1.25 µL NBXX barcode, 5 µL Blunt/TA Ligase Master Mix, and 2.75 µL nuclease‑free water (total 10 µL). Use one native barcode per sample; at least 12 barcodes are required per library.

steps.title: Barcode ligation incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the barcode ligation reactions at room temperature for 20 min.

steps.title: Add EDTA to stop ligation
steps.instruction: Add EDTA to each reaction: 1 µL for tubes with clear caps, 2 µL for tubes with blue caps (cap colour supplied by ONT). Mix thoroughly. Alternatively, inactivate the ligase by heating at 65 °C for the recommended time (per ONT protocol).

steps.title: Pool barcoded reactions
steps.instruction: Pool the barcoding reactions according to the number of samples: 10 µL each for 12–24 samples, 5 µL each for 48 samples, or 2.5 µL each for 96 samples, ensuring the total pooled volume does not exceed 240 µL.

steps.title: Ampure bead cleanup (1.5×)
steps.instruction: Add Ampure beads (supplied with ONT kit) to the pooled barcoded sample at a 1.5× ratio (e.g., for 240 µL pooled sample add 240 µL water and 720 µL beads). Mix thoroughly.

steps.title: Equal‑volume water addition
steps.instruction: Determine the volume of pooled barcoded sample and add an equal volume of nuclease‑free water.

steps.title: Incubate bead mixture
steps.instruction: Vortex briefly, pulse‑centrifuge to collect liquid, then incubate 5 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Magnetic separation (post‑cleanup)
steps.instruction: Place on a magnetic rack for 2 min (or until clear), then carefully discard the supernatant without disturbing the beads.

steps.title: First SFB wash
steps.instruction: Add 250 µL Short Fragment Buffer (SFB), resuspend beads completely by pipette mixing, pulse‑centrifuge, place on magnet, and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Second SFB wash
steps.instruction: Repeat the SFB wash exactly as above; do not air‑dry after this wash.

steps.title: Ethanol wash after SFB
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL room‑temperature 70 % ethanol to the bead pellet, bathe the pellet, then discard the ethanol without touching the beads. Perform only a single 70 % ethanol wash at this stage.

steps.title: Remove residual ethanol
steps.instruction: Pulse‑centrifuge, then remove as much residual ethanol as possible with a P10 pipette.

steps.title: Air‑dry final pellet
steps.instruction: With the tube lid open, incubate 3 min (or until the pellet loses its shine). Very large pellets may require longer; avoid over‑drying which can cause cracking.

steps.title: Elute library DNA
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried bead pellet in 31 µL nuclease‑free water, mix gently by flicking or pipetting, and incubate 2 min at room temperature. If beads were split between two tubes, combine them now to reach a total of 31 µL.

steps.title: Collect final library
steps.instruction: Place the tube on a magnetic rack until clear, then transfer the supernatant (final library) to a clean 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube, ensuring no beads are transferred.

steps.title: Set up native adapter ligation
steps.instruction: Prepare the Native Adapter (NA) ligation reaction according to the ONT protocol (components as supplied).

steps.title: Native adapter incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the NA ligation mixture at room temperature for 20 min.

steps.title: NA bead cleanup (first)
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL Ampure beads (ONT kit) to the NA ligation reaction, mix, and incubate 5 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Magnetic separation (NA cleanup)
steps.instruction: Place on magnetic rack for 2 min, then discard the supernatant without disturbing the beads.

steps.title: First NA SFB wash
steps.instruction: Add 250 µL SFB, resuspend beads completely, pulse‑centrifuge, place on magnet, and discard supernatant.

steps.title: Second NA SFB wash
steps.instruction: Repeat the SFB wash exactly as above; no air‑drying required.

steps.title: Elute NA library
steps.instruction: Resuspend the final bead pellet in 15 µL Elution Buffer (EB, ONT), mix gently, and incubate 2 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Collect NA library
steps.instruction: Place on magnetic rack, allow beads to separate, then transfer the supernatant (final library) to a clean 1.5 mL tube, avoiding any beads.

steps.title: Perform flow cell check
steps.instruction: Open MinKNOW, connect the MinION to the laptop, open the flow‑cell lid, slide the flow cell under the clip, press firmly to ensure proper thermal/electrical contact, then click “Flow Cell Check” in MinKNOW.

steps.title: Prepare priming mix
steps.instruction: In the Flow Cell Flush (FCF) tube combine 1170 µL Flow Cell Flush (FCF), 5 µL BSA (50 mg/mL), and 30 µL Flow Cell Tether (FCT). Mix by inverting and pipette‑mix at room temperature to a final volume of 1205 µL.

steps.title: Open priming port
steps.instruction: Rotate the flow‑cell priming port cover clockwise to open the priming port.

steps.title: Draw back priming buffer
steps.instruction: Set a P1000 pipette to 200 µL, insert the tip into the priming port, turn the wheel until the dial reads 220–230 µL, and draw back 20–30 µL (or until a small volume of buffer enters the tip).

steps.title: Verify buffer flow
steps.instruction: Visually confirm continuous buffer flow from the priming port across the sensor array.

steps.title: Load priming mix
steps.instruction: Load 800 µL of the priming mix into the flow cell via the priming port, avoiding air bubbles. Wait 5 min while preparing the library for loading.

steps.title: Prepare library for loading
steps.instruction: In a new 1.5 mL LoBind tube combine 37.5 µL Sequencing Buffer (SB), 25.5 µL Library Beads (LIB, mixed immediately before use), and 12 µL DNA library plus water (total 75 µL).

steps.title: Complete flow cell priming
steps.instruction: Load 200 µL of the priming mix into the flow‑cell priming port (not the SpotON sample port), avoiding air bubbles.

steps.title: Mix library before loading
steps.instruction: Gently mix the prepared library by pipetting just prior to loading.

steps.title: Load library onto flow cell
steps.instruction: Add approximately half of the library (~37.5 µL) to the SpotON sample port dropwise, ensuring each drop enters before adding the next. Resuspend beads/library and add the second half dropwise.

steps.title: Seal flow cell ports
steps.instruction: Gently replace the SpotON sample port cover, making sure the bung enters the port, and close the priming port.

steps.title: Close device and shield
steps.instruction: Place the light shield onto the flow cell and close the MinION device lid.

steps.title: Quantify final library
steps.instruction: Quantify the final library using a fluorometer (Qubit or Quatus). Expected concentration is 2–9 ng/µL; aim for ~15 ng total library for maximum run yield. Store the library at 4 °C for up to one week if not used immediately.

steps.title: Start sequencing run
steps.instruction: Launch MinKNOW, start the sequencing run, and if live basecalling is selected, enable double‑ended barcoding in the basecalling settings.
